title: Peer response overlap gave no clear cleft volume relation after cell and pair controls in one MICrONS mouse
abstract: We tested whether an axon assigns greater total synapse cleft volume to targets whose movie responses overlap with its other targets. We used 7,979 connected pairs from 117 source cells and 4,772 target cells in the linked MICrONS v1 tables from one mouse. A multiplicative mean model included separate source and target cell effects, direct response similarity, and pair geometry. Fitted source and target weight totals matched observed totals. The primary estimate was 6.02 percent larger volume per standard deviation of peer response overlap, with a nominal 95 percent dyadic interval from 2.44 percent smaller to 15.21 percent larger. All planned full-control sensitivity intervals included no change. Removing each source kept positive point estimates. An independent solver matched the primary log coefficient within 1.82e-10. The result leaves a weight allocation relation unresolved after the stated controls. It does not refute an earlier weighted dimension result, which used a different statistic and reference. One animal, partial tissue, selected connections, measured trial means, sparse cell effects and approximate conditional uncertainty limit inference. We provide original code, a figure, aggregate results, source hashes and retrieval steps. External raw data and derived records stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Cell and pair controls leave a relation between peer response overlap and total cleft volume uncertain in one MICrONS mouse. Points are estimates per standard deviation. Bars are nominal 95 percent dyadic intervals. They do not describe variation across animals.

citations.reason: Tests its stated target incoming weight limitation with a new cell-adjusted mean model. Uses its 117-source cohort rule and dimension framework, but no code or numerical arrays.
Prior target-group response dimension study. This report tests weights within fixed target groups.
Uses its published cell-effect graph support and dyadic uncertainty design as context. New code and a new group-overlap predictor are used.
Ding and colleagues provide the linked v1 analysis tables and prior pair and common-input findings.
MICrONS Consortium source resource with linked neural activity and electron microscopy.
